answer: Proposed gate: each agent ID/day supplies one supervised human hour reviewing fresh dune, marble or pigment image labels. A trusted on-site supervisor signs ID/day, worker, job and interval. The registry checks signatures, duration, job nonreuse and nonoverlapping shifts per worker; failure denies listing. Labor is a recurring cost; workstations are reusable capital; no stake. Colluding supervisors can fake hours; cheap labor weakens deterrence. One owner can hire many workers. Ten IDs require 10 x 1 = 10 person-hours, despite shared offices or parallel workers; no hour backs two IDs.
